In this Review, we outline recent developments in this rapidly advancing field and discuss what lays ahead in order to bring spatially and temporally resolved imaging of subcellular mechanics into a quantitative and broadly accessible framework for cell biology.

title: High-performance HfLaO/InGaCdO transistors with gate-controlled dual plasticity.
abstract: Neuromorphic systems are increasingly moving toward integrating multiple operating modes into a single device. However, existing oxide-based optoelectronic synapses typically rely on pulse strength to switch from short-term plasticity (STP) to long-term plasticity (LTP), which limits the adaptability of a single device to different computational tasks. Here, high-performance HfLaO (HLO)/InGaCdO (IGCO) optoelectronic synaptic transistors are fabricated via full magnetron sputtering, with a steep subthreshold swing (SS) of 96 mV decade-1 and an ultrahigh on/off ratio of 2 × 108. Reversible switching between STP and LTP is realized through gate bias tuning under fixed optical excitation without electrical performance degradation. Stable discrete multilevel conductance states are acquired under an ultralow read voltage of 1 mV and 0.0645 mW cm-2 optical pulses, which supports low-power fully connected neural networks for high-accuracy MNIST handwritten digit recognition. Negative gate bias reproduces typical STP characteristics including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), and gate-adjustable STP relaxation dynamics construct in-sensor physical reservoirs for temporal signal analysis and four-frame human motion recognition. This all-inorganic oxide transistor exhibits exceptionally high electrical performance and operates at low power, while integrating dual synaptic modes to perform trajectory recognition and speech command recognition. It overcomes the limitations of conventional single-modulation strategies and provides practical hardware solutions for low-power multimodal devices.

title: Bladder instillation cocktail for preventing catheter-related bladder discomfort after gynecologic surgery: A randomized controlled trial.
journal: The Journal of international medical research
abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the effectiveness of intravesical instillation of a drug cocktail in preventing postoperative catheter-related bladder discomfort.MethodsIn total, 112 patients were randomized into the "cocktail" or control group. Twenty minutes before the end of the surgery, the "cocktail" group received intravesical instillation of the "cocktail," which contained 1 ug/kg of dexmedetomidine, 5 g of magnesium sulfate, and 10 mg of dexamethasone, totaling 30 mL, while the control group was infused with 30 ml of normal saline. The catheter-related bladder discomfort and visual analog scale of the patients were recorded at 0, 1, 2, and 6 h postoperatively. The 15-item Quality of Recovery scale was used 24 h after surgery to assess the patient's postoperative recovery status.ResultsThe "cocktail" group exhibited significantly decreased catheter-related bladder discomfort severity at 0, 1, 2, and 6 h postoperatively (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, p < 0.001, and p < 0.001, respectively). For the primary outcome (any catheter-related bladder discomfort at 1 h), the risk ratio was 0.52 (95% confidence interval 0.37 to 0.72). Specifically, compared with the control group, the "cocktail" group exhibited a significant decrease in moderate-to-severe catheter-related bladder discomfort at 0, 1, and 2 h postoperatively (5 (8.9%) vs. 13 (23.2%), p = 0.040; 6 (10.7%) vs. 14 (25.0%), p = 0.048; 4 (7.1%) vs. 12 (21.4%), p = 0.031) with rate ratio 0.33-0.43 (95% confidence interval 0.11 to 0.99). Rescue tramadol dose was significantly lower in the cocktail group (35 ± 8 vs 50 ± 12 mg, p = 0.002; median difference = -15.0 mg, 95% confidence interval -19.2 to -10.8).Moreover, patients in the "cocktail" group exhibited significantly higher postoperative recovery scale scores than those in the control group (median difference = 9.0, 95% confidence interval: 7.0-11.0, p < 0.001).ConclusionBladder instillation of the "cocktail" significantly reduces the severity and incidence of moderate-to-severe catheter-related bladder discomfort and improves postoperative recovery in gynecologic patients.

title: Creatine and CoQ10 with physical activity on muscle function in children with myositis: a proof-of-concept trial.
abstract: We aimed to evaluate whether Creatine (Cr) and Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation, combined with a self-paced physical activity program, enhances muscle function in juvenile idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (JIIM). Fifteen participants, (8 male/ 7 female) aged 9-17, from SickKids' JIIM clinic were recruited for a double-blinded, placebo-controlled, randomized, multiple-baseline trial. All participants participated in both the placebo and intervention periods. The primary outcome, muscle function, was measured by the Wingate Test. Secondary outcomes included improvements in jumping height, disease activity, and quality of life. There was a significant increase in peak power (mean difference (MD)=95 Watts; p = 0.02), mean power (MD = 74 Watts; p = 0.02), and minimum power (MD = 47 Watts; p = 0.01) in the intervention periods compared to placebo periods. Vertical jump peak power also increased significantly in the intervention period (MD = 493 Watts; p = 0.02). However, these significant findings were not replicated in the prespecified sensitivity analyses, which incorporated linear mixed models to adjust for individual baseline values. Cr+CoQ10 supplementation combined with physical activity showed positive effects; however, these findings may be attributable to chance imbalances in baseline values. Alternatively, the lack of statistical significance in the sensitivity analyses may reflect a Type II error, as the study size was set for the more powerful primary analysis. Further research is necessary to fully understand the impact of Cr and CoQ10 supplementation in children with JIIM. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04286178.

title: Loss of spermine synthase recapitulates RAS/MAPK and sensory processing phenotypes of Drosophila RASopathy models.
abstract: Hyperactivation of RAS/MAPK signaling is a hallmark of RASopathies, genetic developmental conditions associated with cognitive and sensory processing impairments. Genes linked to this pathway have been reported to be enriched among Drosophila models with habituation deficits, a behavioral phenotype reflecting impaired sensory filtering. To investigate whether RAS/MAPK overactivation extends beyond classical RASopathies, we generated 89 and screened 41 viable habituation deficient Drosophila RNAi models, measuring pathway activity as an increased phosphorylated ERK to ERK ratio. This screen identified Sms, the ortholog of human spermine synthase (SMS), implicated in Snyder-Robinson syndrome. RAS/MAPK overactivation along with hyperreactivity and habituation impairments were confirmed in a full loss-of-function mutant. An RNAi screen targeting polyamine pathway genes identified Sat (human SAT1/2, SATL1), with independent models reproducing aspects of these phenotypes. Knockdown of Sms or Sat in GABAergic neurons impaired habituation, suggesting a role for polyamine metabolism in inhibitory circuit function. These findings reveal previously unrecognized convergence between polyamine dysregulation and RASopathies, raising the possibility for shared therapeutic opportunities through modulation of either pathway.

title: Glymphatic Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, with hallmark pathological features including amyloid-beta plaques, tau tangles, and neuronal loss. The glymphatic system, a recently discovered network responsible for brain waste clearance, plays a crucial role in maintaining cerebral homeostasis by facilitating the removal of neurotoxic metabolites, including amyloid-beta. Disruption of glymphatic function has emerged as a key factor in AD pathophysiology, contributing to the accumulation of toxic proteins and accelerating neurodegenerative processes. This narrative review explores the complex interplay between glymphatic dysfunction and AD. We discuss the mechanisms of the glymphatic system, emphasizing its reliance on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial fluid flow to clear metabolic waste, and how this process is closely linked to sleep cycles. In AD, impaired glymphatic function, exacerbated by aging and sleep disturbances, accelerates the buildup of amyloid-beta and tau, driving neurodegeneration. Furthermore, sleep disturbances commonly observed in AD patients further hinder glymphatic activity, creating a vicious cycle that exacerbates cognitive decline. Emerging therapeutic approaches aimed at enhancing glymphatic function-including sleep regulation, pharmacological agents, and lifestyle interventions-are promising, but most findings remain preliminary and largely based on animal studies or early clinical observations. These strategies should therefore be considered exploratory until validated in large-scale human trials. By restoring efficient waste clearance, such interventions may offer novel avenues for slowing or preventing AD progression.

title: Animal and Cell Models in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease: Current Innovations Reviewed.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) remain major global health challenges due to their complex pathology and lack of curative therapies. Advancing therapeutic strategies requires reliable experimental models that recapitulate disease mechanisms. This review summarizes recent developments in animal and in vitro models for AD and PD, with emphasis on their translational relevance and applications. Transgenic mice (APP/PS1, 3xTg-AD), α-synuclein and LRRK2-based models for PD, rat 6- OHDA systems, zebrafish, and non-human primates provide valuable insights into amyloid deposition, tau aggregation, synaptic dysfunction, and motor impairment, though each presents limitations in faithfully mimicking human disease. Complementary in vitro approaches using neuronal and glial cell lines enable targeted studies on oxidative stress, inflammation, amyloid-beta (Aβ) toxicity, tau pathology, and dopaminergic degeneration. Emerging platforms such as CRISPR/Cas9-based editing, induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived organoids, and artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery are further expanding the preclinical landscape. Together, these integrated strategies enhance understanding of neurodegenerative processes and hold promise for the development of effective disease-modifying therapies.

title: A Correlative Light and Electron Microscopy Workflow for Nanoscale Three-Dimensional Reconstruction of Synaptic Projections From the Thalamic Reticular Nucleus.
abstract: Correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) combines molecular specificity with nanoscale ultrastructural resolution and has become an important approach for investigating neural circuit organization. However, ultrastructural reconstruction of long-range projection terminals remains technically challenging. This study aimed to develop a CLEM workflow for the identification, localization, three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, and ultrastructural characterization of thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN)-derived presynaptic terminals in the mouse thalamus. TRN presynaptic terminals were selectively labeled by stereotaxic injection of rAAV-hSyn-Synaptophysin-mCherry. Confocal microscopy was combined with serial section scanning electron microscopy (ssSEM) to achieve fluorescence-guided ultrastructural imaging and 3D reconstruction of labeled axonal boutons and synaptic contacts. The CLEM workflow enabled fluorescence-guided identification of presynaptic terminals within serial EM datasets. 3D reconstruction of a representative TRN axon segment revealed multiple en passant boutons along continuous axonal shafts. Ultrastructural analysis demonstrated synaptic contacts with multiple postsynaptic dendritic profiles, together with distinct vesicle distributions and mitochondrial organization within presynaptic boutons. This study presents a practical CLEM-based workflow for nanoscale reconstruction of long-range synaptic projections. Application of this method to the TRN-to-thalamus pathway illustrates the spatial organization of presynaptic boutons and their postsynaptic contacts in the thalamic neuropil. The workflow provides a methodological framework for ultrastructural studies of defined neural projections in the mammalian brain.

title: The Diagnostic Dilemma of Acute Vestibular Syndrome: Why HINTS Outperforms Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging?
abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic approaches, specifically the comparative accuracy of bedside clinical examinations versus early neuroimaging, in differentiating central from peripheral causes of Acute Vestibular Syndrome (AVS). A comprehensive narrative literature review was conducted utilizing established scientific databases, including PubMed/Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase, covering articles published up to 2024. A structured search strategy was applied using keywords such as "Acute Vestibular Syndrome", "Central vestibular dysfunction", "Peripheral vestibular dysfunction", and "HINTS protocol". Peer-reviewed clinical trials, mechanistic studies, and authoritative guidelines were included to synthesize the current evidence regarding the diagnosis and management of acute vertigo. The synthesis of the literature reveals that targeted bedside neuro-otological examinations demonstrate superior sensitivity (96.8%) and specificity (98.5%) compared to early "Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging" in detecting posterior circulation strokes within the initial 48 hours. Early neuroimaging frequently yields false-negative results in up to 14.3% of ischemic events. Accurate differentiation of etiologies in continuous vertigo relies heavily on structured bedside clinical assessments rather than immediate neuroimaging. Implementing these clinical protocols prevents severe neurological sequelae from missed posterior fossa strokes while simultaneously avoiding unnecessary healthcare expenditures for benign peripheral conditions.

title: Ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage in the post-acute phase after myocardial infarction: a nationwide cohort study in Sweden.
abstract: Patients who survive myocardial infarction (MI) remain at risk of stroke in the post-acute MI-phase, after discharge. We investigated the incidence of ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage in MI survivors attending early follow-up. We included MI survivors from the SWEDEHEART registry linked to national health registers, who attended a cardiac rehabilitation visit 6-10 weeks post-MI between 2005 and 2020 and followed them until 31 December 2021. Fine-Grey competing-risk regression was used to assess associations between clinical factors and stroke outcomes. Among 85,360 MI survivors, 4275 patients experienced ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage during follow-up. The incidence of ischaemic stroke was highest during the first year after MI (~1.1%) and declined thereafter, while intracerebral haemorrhage remained rare throughout follow-up. Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was independently associated with higher ischaemic stroke risk. Compared with normal LVEF, patients with moderately reduced LVEF (30%-39%) had an sHR of 1.47 (95% CI, 1.14-1.90) at 1 year and 1.47 (95% CI, 1.25-1.74) at 5 years, while those with severely reduced LVEF (<30%) had an sHR of 1.62 (95% CI, 1.11-2.35) at 1 year and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.02-1.71) at 5 years. Atrial fibrillation (AF) was strongly and independently associated with ischaemic stroke risk (sHR 2.21; 95% CI, 1.70-2.88 at 1 year; sHR 1.54; 95% CI, 1.28-1.84 at 5 years). While oral anticoagulation alone was not associated with reduced stroke risk, it was associated with significantly lower ischaemic stroke risk among patients with AF (AF × oral anticoagulant interaction sHR 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.75 at 1 year). Stroke risk after MI is highest during the first year and is strongly influenced by AF presence and reduced LVEF. These findings highlight the importance of early risk stratification and targeted prevention strategies after MI.

title: Platelets in Alzheimer's disease: pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
abstract: This review examines the role of platelets, the primary peripheral source of amyloid precursor protein (APP) and amyloid-beta (Aβ), in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, focusing on the bidirectional feedback loop between peripheral platelet over-activation and central neuropathology, alongside potential antiplatelet therapies. A narrative review was conducted evaluating literature on platelet biological functions, pathological shifts in platelet APP processing in AD, mechanisms of blood-brain barrier (BBB) breakdown, and the therapeutic potential of antiplatelet agents (e.g. aspirin, clopidogrel) and adenosine A2A receptor modulators. In AD patients, platelet APP expression is markedly upregulated, shifting toward amyloidogenic processing via decreased α-secretase and increased β-secretase activity. Activated platelets breach the BBB, release pro-inflammatory mediators into the brain parenchyma, and promote cerebral Aβ deposition. Reciprocally, central AD pathology further drives systemic platelet activation, creating a self-reinforcing disease loop. A clear, bidirectional relationship may exist between activated platelets and AD neuropathology. Because peripheral platelets actively fuel central amyloid accumulation and neuroinflammation, targeting platelet activation may be a viable strategy to mitigate AD risk and slow disease progression.

title: Beethoven's progressive hearing loss: Neuroplasticity and musical adaptation.
journal: Journal of the history of the neurosciences
abstract: Ludwig van Beethoven's sustained musical productivity despite progressive hearing loss represents one of the most remarkable historical examples of adaptation to auditory deprivation. By integrating historical documents, personal correspondence, and musicological analyses, this paper evaluates these internal mechanisms within an audiological and neuroplasticity-oriented framework. The findings indicate that his creative output was potentially supported by vibration perception, motor memory, visual feedback, and internal auditory imagery. These observations suggest that Beethoven's late works may reflect cross-modal neuroplasticity and somatosensory integration processes independent of auditory feedback. Ultimately, understanding these mechanisms may contribute to clinical perspectives on auditory rehabilitation, hearing loss adaptation, and patient-centered management strategies in individuals with severe hearing impairment.

title: A Mixed Methods Approach to Implementing the Canadian Spinal Bulbar Muscular Atrophy Guideline.
journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
abstract: Spinal bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA) is an X-linked neuromuscular disease that disproportionately affects Indigenous people in Canada. The first Canadian guidelines for the management of SBMA were recently published. There is limited guidance from the literature to inform optimal implementation strategies. A mixed methods approach was used to determine SBMA guideline implementation strategies. A combination of activities (surveys, roundtable discussion, modified Delphi consensus exercise with experts, Indigenous engagement) was employed to gather opinions from multiple stakeholders and experts (physicians, allied healthcare providers, people with living experience [PWLE] including Indigenous people and patient organizations). Barriers to guideline implementation included lack of awareness of the disease and the need for comprehensive multidisciplinary teams to address the multisystem symptoms and complications of SBMA. A survey of current practice patterns demonstrated several areas for improvement, including attention to cardiac symptoms, laryngospasm and care for female carriers. Roundtable discussion with health experts and patient advocacy groups centered on the following themes: (1) awareness, (2) resources, (3) knowledge translation and (4) policy support. The Indigenous engagement process with the community guiding circle emphasized the need for ongoing involvement of PWLE, Indigenous communities, leaders and health networks in the implementation process. The modified Delphi process with physician experts led to the development of specific implementation strategies, with emphasis on education for healthcare providers and PWLE, including the development of written materials. Intentional partnerships with PWLE, Indigenous communities, patient organizations and healthcare professionals are essential to meaningful guideline implementation.

title: Successful archetype JC polyomavirus infection in hiPSC-derived neural culture of astrocytes and neurons.
abstract: JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) is the causative agent of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a fatal neurodegenerative disease in immunocompromised individuals. JCPyV is a strictly human pathogen, and animal models are inappropriate to fully reproduce human disease. PML is often associated with neurotropic JCPyV variants harboring rearrangements within the non-coding regulatory region (NCCR) and VP1 capsid protein gene. However, archetype virus has also been identified in the brain and its association with PML cannot be excluded. To assess the ability of archetype virus to infect neural cells and to explore the cellular effects of JCPyV infection, we performed experimental 35-day infections in neural cell cultures consisting of astrocytes and neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC). Archetype JCPyV infection was successfully established in both astrocytes and neurons at comparable rates. Infection in neurons supports our previous observations from brain tissue of PML patients, suggesting that neurons are also true target cells of JCPyV infection. Minor neurotropic variants emerged in the course of infection. RNA sequencing revealed significant regulation of genes implicated in cell cycle, DNA replication and repair, and cell division. The observed remarkable regulation of gene expression was proposedly driven by viral large T antigen, pRb and E2F family transcription factors, with consequent enhancement of JCPyV replication. Our neural cell model reproduced many observations from PML brain tissue, suggesting that the model is appropriate to study key cellular events and the pathogenesis of JCPyV in neurodegeneration.

title: Interpreting Acupuncture-Specific Neuroplasticity in Poststroke Motor Recovery: Statistical and Methodological Considerations.
VRCycle: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Virtual Reality Cycling Intervention in People With Knee Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Exercise is recommended as a core treatment for knee osteoarthritis; yet uptake is suboptimal, with identified barriers including pain, difficulty (overly effortful), and boredom. Virtual reality (VR) shows promise in overcoming these barriers, although whether VR-enhanced exercise is acceptable to people with osteoarthritis and feasible in physical therapy settings is unknown. The objective was to assess the feasibility of conducting a clinical trial to evaluate VR-enhanced cycling and explore preliminary efficacy of this intervention. A prospectively registered (ACTRN12624000122550), two-arm feasibility randomized controlled trial was conducted. The trial was conducted at a clinical trials facility. Forty-one participants with painful knee osteoarthritis were enrolled. Participants were randomized (1:1 ratio) to receive VR-enhanced cycling or traditional (no-VR) cycling, both involving twelve, 30-minute cycling sessions over 6-weeks, supervised by a physical therapist. A priori feasibility criteria surrounding recruitment and enrolment rate, intervention adherence, technical difficulty, retention, and participant experience (acceptability, credibility, adverse events) were evaluated. Clinical outcomes (pain, function) and exercise capacity (perceptually regulated exercise test) were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, 1-month follow-up (clinical outcomes only). Within-session exercise engagement (work, time) and experience (perceived exertion, affect) were evaluated as process variables. All feasibility criteria were met. An average of 6.8 participants per week were eligible with a 73% enrollment rate. Participants attended 91% of intervention sessions, and 90% of participants completed follow-up assessments. VR technical issues were rare (3% of sessions) as were adverse events (2 unrelated to VR). Treatment acceptability and credibility was high and clinical outcomes improved in both groups. Progression to a full trial is supported due to high feasibility, acceptability, and improvement in clinical outcomes. Although not powered to evaluate efficacy, the within-group changes observed demonstrate that both cycling modalities can improve knee pain, function, and exercise capacity.

title: Extended-Dose Letrozole Regimen versus Standard-Dose Regimen for Ovulation Induction and Biochemical Pregnancy in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
abstract: To compare the extended-dose letrozole regimen with the standard-dose regimen for ovulation induction and biochemical pregnancy in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). A randomised controlled trial. Place and Duration of the Study: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Sir Gangaram Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, from April to September 2025. A total of 174 women with PCOS were randomised into extended-dose (n = 87; letrozole 5 mg, cycle days 2-10) and standard- dose (n = 87; letrozole 5 mg, cycle days 2-6) groups. Ovulation was triggered with human chorionic gonadotropin (5000 IU) upon detecting mature follicles (18-22 mm). Ovulation induction was confirmed by measuring mid-luteal serum progesterone levels on day 21, and biochemical pregnancy by urine pregnancy test on day 28. Statistical analysis was performed using both univariable and multivariable logistic regression frameworks to estimate odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Baseline demographics and endocrine parameters were comparable, with no statistically significant differences between groups (all p >0.05). The extended-dose letrozole regimen achieved significantly higher rates and odds of successful ovulation induction (69.0% vs. 51.7%, p = 0.020; aOR = 1.995, p = 0.035) and positive biochemical pregnancy (33.3% vs. 16.1%, p = 0.008; aOR = 2.500, p = 0.014) than the standard protocol. Conversely, secondary subfertility independently reduced the likelihood of successful ovulation induction (aOR = 0.472, p = 0.026). None of the other evaluated covariates showed a significant association in both univariable and multivariable analyses. Extended-dose letrozole regimen demonstrated better efficacy in achieving successful ovulation induction and biochemical pregnancy compared with the standard-dose regimen. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution in light of the study's inherent limitations. Letrozole, Infertility, Ovulation induction, Polycystic ovary syndrome, Pregnancy.

title: Cryo-EM structures of an anti-MLC1 Fab in apo and peptide-bound states reveal the basis of antigen recognition.
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies are widely used to detect and characterize membrane proteins, yet for most such reagents, the molecular basis of target recognition remains structurally undefined. Here, we report the structural and biochemical characterization of 37E5, a monoclonal antibody that recognizes MLC1, an astrocytic membrane protein implicated in gliovascular homeostasis and megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy with subcortical cysts. 37E5 specifically detects endogenous MLC1 across multiple experimental systems, including brain lysates and mouse and human brain tissues, and binds purified human MLC1 with nanomolar affinity as determined by biolayer interferometry. To define the molecular basis of recognition, we determined 3.2 and 3.0 Å cryo-EM structures of the 37E5 Fab in apo and antigen-bound states, respectively. The antigen-bound structure revealed continuous density for an MLC1-derived peptide within the paratope, stabilized by coordinated hydrogen-bonding, ionic, and hydrophobic interactions. Structural comparison between apo and bound states showed localized conformational changes confined to the complementarity-determining regions, consistent with a restrained, local induced-fit adjustment of the paratope; because these backbone deviations are small, they are interpreted only in the context of the coordinate uncertainty expected at this resolution. Comparative analyses further explained species-dependent recognition through sequence variation at key epitope residues, corroborated by binding assays across four MLC1 orthologs. These findings define the structural basis of selective MLC1 recognition by 37E5 and illustrate, for this antibody-peptide pair, how experimental cryo-EM structures complement AI-based prediction methods by resolving peptide orientation and interaction geometry at the antibody-antigen interface.

title: Mapping myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD): A global review of publicly listed patient disease registries and databases.
abstract: Real-world data are crucial to improving care for patients with rare diseases. To develop the first global map of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) patient registries/databases. Registries/databases were identified through rare disease portals, registry websites, and other sources, and surveyed. Of the respondents (N = 26), the majority were established within the past 15 years and reported being self-funded. Most collect diagnostic, clinical, and laboratory data. Major objectives included supporting scientific research and advancing disease understanding. Despite cost, time, resource, and data quality challenges, registries/databases provide important insights into addressing unmet needs in MOGAD and NMOSD.

title: An MRI template of the female C57Bl/6N mouse brain.
abstract: Brain templates are pivotal tools for standardized image analysis and interpretation in neuroimaging studies. However, matching data and reference remains essential. With growing awareness of sex as a relevant biological variable and male-centric biases in past medical investigations, the continuous limited use and availability of female-specific brain templates, particularly in preclinical research are alarming. To address this gap in preclinical neuroimaging, we created a high-resolution, in vivo structural MRI brain template for female C57Bl/6N mice, a population-average derived from 153 axial and coronal scans of 80 female mice. We further analyzed the template's characteristics regarding the achieved effective resolution and compared it to currently available standard brains. Validation was performed by spatially normalizing external data to established templates and the novel reference, contrasting the degree of deformation. We present a readily applicable and accessible set of files (structural images, tissue probability maps, anatomical annotations, and transformation matrices) as reference for female-centric neuroimaging research questions. The novel template brain exhibits high nominal and effective resolution, differs significantly in spatial and cohort characteristics from previous references and shows improved performance with external data of female mice. We propose that integrating sex-specific tools into preclinical neuroimaging studies is essential for reducing sex bias, enhancing data reproducibility and strengthening the translational validity of neuroscientific findings. Research further disentangling (sub-)strain- and sex-differences is warranted.

title: Impact of 5-alpha reductase inhibitors on pre-biopsy MRI interpretation: effects on PI-RADS assessment and local staging.
abstract: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs) are widely prescribed for the management of benign prostatic hyperplasia and are known to induce morphological and metabolic changes in prostatic tissue. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the impact of 5-ARI therapy on multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) findings and the potential clinical implications. While some studies report reduced discrimination on T2-weighted and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) metrics after long-term exposure, others suggest improved lesion visibility due to a more homogeneous benign background. Most studies found no significant difference in the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) lesion distribution between 5-ARI users and non-users. However, conflicting evidence exists regarding mpMRI sensitivity and specificity in 5-ARI-treated patients. Limited data is available on the effect of 5-ARIs on local staging accuracy. Overall, the effect of 5-ARIs on prostate mpMRI interpretation appears complex, highlighting the need for prospective studies and treatment-adjusted risk assessment tools to support clinical decision-making.

title: Ecological assessment of executive functions and reasoning in Colombian children: cross-validation and measurement invariance of the Spanish CORE-6/10.
journal: Child neuropsychology : a journal on normal and abnormal development in childhood and adolescence
abstract: Ecological assessment of executive function (EF) in children relies heavily on informant-report instruments that rarely include logical-abstract reasoning, while culturally grounded measures developed originally in Spanish for Latin American populations remain scarce. This study examined the psychometric structure, internal cross-validation, and measurement invariance of the CORE-6/10, a Spanish-language informant-report instrument for children aged 6-10 years assessing five executive domains and two naturalistic reasoning dimensions: verbal-logical and perceptual-analytical reasoning. Validation used non-overlapping calibration and confirmation subsamples (N = 391; EFA: n = 195; CFA: n = 196), polychoric matrices, parallel analysis, ULS oblimin EFA, and WLSMV CFA; invariance was tested across sex, age, and informant type. The seven correlated-factor model was retained as the best-fitting admissible solution (CFI = .940, TLI = .935, RMSEA = .049, SRMR = .081). An exploratory bifactor analysis suggested substantial general-factor saturation (ωh = .71; ECV = .50), although estimation anomalies precluded treating it as a primary confirmatory model. Internal consistency was adequate (ordinal α = .76-.87), with change-based evidence consistent with approximate scalar invariance across comparisons (|ΔCFI| ≤.005). Reasoning dimensions showed general-factor loadings (.476-.735) comparable to core EF domains, suggesting shared variance with general executive functioning while retaining domain-specific variance. Findings support the empirical relevance of reasoning within this ecological measurement framework and the CORE-6/10 as a promising culturally grounded instrument for research in Colombian children, with potential future applications in school-based screening pending independent replication, multimethod validation, normative development, and evidence of classification accuracy.

title: Are we moving forward from amisulpride? LB-102 (N-methyl amisulpride) in acute schizophrenia.
abstract: Schizophrenia has a low prevalence but a high health burden. Although used in schizophrenia, amisulpride has limited blood-brain barrier penetration. LB-102 (N-methylated amisulpride) maintains the ability to antagonize D2- and 5-HT7-receptors with longer receptor occupancies than amisulpride. A phase 2 clinical trial (NOVA) has showed that LB-102 has some efficacy in acute schizophrenia, but this comes with adverse events, such as increased prolactin levels, that need further investigation. The inpatient setting of NOVA may have contributed to the improvement observed with LB-102. Based on NOVA, LB Pharmaceutics have moved LB-102 into phase 3 for the treatment of acute exacerbations of schizophrenia. Like NOVA, the participants of NOVA2 will be inpatients. Consequently, this trial will not address the issue of whether LB-102 is effective in the outpatient setting, and these needs testing. A recently approved new approach to treating schizophrenia is the bitopic M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonist xanomeline. When xanomeline was compared to amisulpride, it ranked lower. In conclusion, further clinical trials are needed to determine whether LB-102 is better than amisulpride and xanomeline in the treatment of schizophrenia in both inpatients and outpatients.

title: Chronic stress disrupts microglial-vascular interaction via AT1R signaling and altered microglial state to drive depression-like behaviors.
abstract: Depression entails a range of pathological processes in the brain, typically characterized by altered microglial state, neural dysfunction, and vascular dysregulation. While it is well established that activated microglia inflict damage to neurons through direct and indirect microglia-neuron interactions, their interaction with vasculature and the associated regulation of vascular structure and function in depression remain poorly understood. Here, using a mouse model of depression induced by chronic unpredictable stress (CUS), we find that in stressed mice, activated microglia present reduced motility and decreased contact area with vasculature, which is accompanied by pathological vascular structure and function, characterized by reduced vessel density, narrowed vascular diameters, and sluggish blood flow velocity. We observe that vascular structure in the stressed mice is rapidly modified by the vessel-associated microglia (VAM). These VAM show upregulated angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) expression, which is not present in the vascular-uncontacted microglia. Furthermore, we demonstrate that AT1R signaling together with altered microglial state under chronic stress are critical mediators for the altered microglia-vascular interactions, vascular dysregulation, as well as the depression-like behaviors. Together, our findings reveal that under CUS, the aberrant microglial-vascular interaction, including the dysregulated microglial vasoregulation arising from AT1R signaling and altered microglial state, leads to depression, forging a new link between chronic stress and depression.

title: Network connectivity and amyloid-β align with tau in atypical Alzheimer disease subtypes.
abstract: Spatiotemporal patterns of tau accumulation differ between Alzheimer disease (AD) subtypes in brain networks related to clinical manifestations. Converging evidence suggests that accumulation may be driven by spreading through network connections and/or interactions with amyloid-β (Aβ). Persons with atypical AD presentations might carry pre-existing network-specific vulnerabilities, which might predispose these areas to tau pathology. However, it is unknown if regional patterns of Aβ and network connectivity differ between tau-defined subtypes and whether these patterns precede tau accumulation. We used Subtype-and-Stage-Inference (SuStaIn) to identify subtypes in 919 tau-PET scans from 709 participants in the Knight ADRC. We tested group differences between tau-defined subtypes in regional Aβ-PET and resting-state-functional-connectivity (RSFC) seed maps to early-stage tau epicenter regions using retrospective imaging data preceding the tau-PET scans by up to 14 years, including across stages of AD progression. Most participants were tau-negative (N = 522). Among tau-positive participants, we identified three tau-PET subtypes. Limbic tau was the most common subtype (N = 136, 73.9%), resembling amnestic AD. Participants with the posterior tau subtype (N = 25, 13.6%) had specific cognitive deficits on visuospatial-dominant tasks, resembling posterior cortical atrophy. Participants with the medial-temporal-lobe-sparing (MTL-sparing) tau subtype (N = 23, 12.5%) were younger and more severely impaired, resembling early-onset dysexecutive AD. Subtype-specific Aβ-PET elevations colocalized with regions of tau accumulation, including in preliminary retrospective analyses of scans preceding tau positivity. RSFC was elevated between subtype-specific regions of tau spreading. Specifically, connectivity was elevated between occipital regions in the posterior tau subtype and was elevated between temporal and frontal regions in the MTL-sparing subtype. In preliminary retrospective analyses, these patterns were detectable in small subsets of scans acquired when participants were Aβ-negative or cognitively unimpaired, before they would later exhibit atypical tau patterns, and extended with disease progression. Regional patterns of Aβ, tau, and functional connectivity align in subtype-specific brain networks. Elevated connectivity between tau spreading regions might indicate network-specific vulnerabilities that predispose these regions to tau aggregation, possibly preceding Aβ positivity. These results suggest a temporal sequence of disease progression in brain networks, which might inform explanations of clinico-pathological heterogeneity and the development of precision medicine tools for early detection, prognosis, and treatment of atypical AD.

title: Reorganization of motor unit discharge-state space during ischemia-assisted fatigue: an energy landscape analysis.
abstract: Neuromuscular fatigue increases variability in motor-unit (MU) discharge and force output, yet how it reorganizes population-level MU discharge dynamics remains poorly understood. Conventional analytical approaches primarily quantify discharge magnitude, variability, and common synaptic input, providing limited information regarding the organization of discharge-state space. Hence, we applied a time-resolved energy landscape framework that preserves a joint representation of the mean and variability of pooled MU discharge to characterize fatigue-related reorganization of population-level MU discharge-state space. This approach was motivated by the premise that force steadiness depends on the joint organization of neural drive level and neural drive variability. Force output and decomposed surface electromyographic signals were recorded during submaximal isometric wrist extension before and after an ischemia-assisted fatigue protocol in forty healthy adults. Thirty-five participants exhibiting post-fatigue reductions in maximal voluntary contraction force were included in subsequent analyses. Pooled MU discharge activity was represented by the instantaneous mean firing rate and analyzed using a sliding-window approach. Energy landscapes were constructed in a two-dimensional discharge-state space defined by the mean and variability of pooled MU discharge activity, enabling quantification of landscape structure (basin number, basin area, and basin depth) and state-space occupancy (centroid location and centroid dispersion). Fatigue significantly increased force fluctuation magnitude (P < 0.001) and altered the organization of MU discharge-state space. Specifically, fatigue increased the number (P = 0.017) and area (P = 0.012) of attractor basins, indicating a broader distribution of preferred discharge configurations. Fatigue also induced significant shifts in centroid location (P ≤ 0.008) and increased centroid dispersion (P = 0.004), reflecting broader occupancy of discharge states. Furthermore, fatigue-related increases in force fluctuation magnitude were positively associated with basin area expansion (r = 0.368, P = 0.030) and centroid dispersion (r = 0.468, P = 0.005). Ischemia-assisted fatigue reorganized the state-space architecture of pooled MU discharge activity, resulting in broader discharge-state occupancy and reduced force steadiness. Energy landscape analysis provides a complementary time-resolved framework that preserves the joint evolution of the mean and variability of pooled MU discharge, offering a novel state-space perspective on fatigue-related decline in force stability.

title: ChatGPT vs. Gemini: could artificial intelligence safely improve the perioperative surgical flow while increasing patient awareness?
journal: International journal of retina and vitreous
abstract: To evaluate the efficiency and safety of ChatGPT and Gemini in the surgical workflow, from patient admission to surgical planning. Twenty questions regarding preoperative and postoperative aspects of vitreoretinal surgery-most frequently asked by patients at our center-were submitted to ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Gemini (Google). Similarly, twenty surgical cases treated at our center were submitted to both platforms. The same questions and cases were evaluated by a panel of vitreoretinal surgeons with varying experience. Primary outcomes were overall reliability and inter-group agreement of the two chatbots; the secondary outcome was their ability to identify cases requiring ophthalmologist intervention. In the clinical case dataset (N = 80), ChatGPT and Gemini performed comparably, with ChatGPT slightly outperforming Gemini in discussion timeliness (p = 0.019). In the patient inquiry dataset (N = 80), Gemini provided more complete, accurate, and timely clinical indications (p ≤ 0.011). Stratified analyses by surgeon experience (Junior vs. Senior) showed consistent evaluations across experience levels. ChatGPT and Gemini perform similarly in clinical case discussions, with ChatGPT slightly better in timeliness. For patient-oriented inquiries, Gemini delivers more accurate, complete, and up-to-date responses. While AI platforms demonstrate potential, their adoption in clinical practice should be preceded by thorough and rigorous evaluation.

title: EMMPRIN-mediated metabolism of monocytes promotes disease progression in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages are increasingly recognized as key contributors to the initiation and progression of inflammatory conditions, in part through metabolic reprogramming that drives pathogenic inflammatory phenotypes. However, the upstream mechanisms that coordinate these early metabolic transitions in multiple sclerosis (MS) remain largely undefined. We previously identified extracellular matrix metalloproteinase inducer (EMMPRIN/CD147), a chaperone of monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4), as a regulator of lactate efflux and glycolysis-dependent activation in murine macrophages. Here, we investigate the role of EMMPRIN in circulating CCR2+ monocytes during experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model for MS. Using the newly generated CCR2CreERT2:EMMPRINfl/fl (CCR2:EMMP-/-) mice, we demonstrate that presymptomatic deletion of EMMPRIN prevents or significantly attenuates clinical disability and is associated with a marked reduction in CNS infiltration by CD45+ leukocytes, including macrophages and T cells. Single cell RNA-sequencing of blood monocytes during pre-onset EAE, combined with proteomic profiling of bone marrow-derived macrophages from CCR2:EMMP-/- mice, reveals coordinated metabolic reprogramming characterized by reduced glycolytic activity, enhanced mitochondrial electron transport, and increased fatty acid oxidation. These data identify EMMPRIN-mediated lactate export as a pivotal regulator of immunometabolic programming in monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages and implicate this pathway as an upstream driver of early neuroinflammatory pathology in MS. Targeting this pathway during presymptomatic phases may therefore represent a promising strategy to prevent disease progression by modulating early inflammatory metabolism.

title: A peripheral proteomic signature of Alzheimer's disease is identified in the plasma extracellular vesicles of mild cognitive impairment patients from a memory clinic: the BIOPEXAL study.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is commonly diagnosed when neuronal damage is already established and irreversible. Achieving an accurate differential diagnosis in the preclinical and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stage is one of the greatest challenges nowadays. Nanotechnological analysis of plasma extracellular vesicles (pEVs) are gaining attention as a promising tool for the early detection of AD pathology. This study aims to evaluate the proteomic profile of pEVs from patients with MCI and AD dementia to explore their potential as AD screening tools. pEVs were isolated by ultracentrifugation from 144 patients with MCI A-T-, MCI A+T+, and AD dementia. Nanoparticle tracking analysis and cryo-TEM were used to characterize the pEVs. CSF, serum and pEVs proteomics were carried out by using the multiplex PEA technology of Olink® proteomics, Inflammation and Neurology Explore 384 panels (768 proteins). Characterization results showed that isolated plasma fraction corresponded in shape, size and concentration to EVs. Many pEVs neurology proteins involved in AD pathology significantly correlated (r > ± 0.30, p < 0.05) with their CSF homonyms, but not with their serum's. pEVs' proteome correlated with common AD signatures (CSF Aβ42 and pTau181, plasma pTau181, MMSE, NBACE, and Qalb) showing similar patterns to those observed with CSF biomarkers. Several pEVs neurology proteins didn't exhibit differences between the MCI A+T+ and AD dementia groups, whilst they did with MCI A-T-. Proteins in pEVs showed strong correlations with several measures of brain atrophy in MRI. Several neurology pEV proteins predicted conversion from MCI to AD dementia. Moreover, some of these showed a significant diagnostic accuracy of AD pathology. Preliminary results suggest that EVs biomarker signature could reflect AD pathology in the prodromal stages of AD continuum. However, further experiments are still needed for a better understanding of EVs' role in AD development and pathology dissemination.

title: Cancer morbidity and mortality in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder: a population-based and sibling cohort study in Sweden and Denmark.
abstract: Assessing the risk of cancer morbidity and mortality in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is important to identify potential disparities in cancer incidence and prognosis. In this study, we aimed to assess the overall and site-specific cancer risk among individuals with OCD, as well as their cancer-specific and all-cause mortality following a cancer diagnosis. This cohort study used population-based matched cohorts and sibling-matched cohorts from Sweden (people born between 1932 and 2010) and Denmark (1932-2009). OCD diagnoses were derived by the Swedish National Patient Register and the Danish Psychiatric Central Register. Each individual with OCD was matched with 20 individuals without OCD on sex, birth year, and calendar time and, in separate analyses, with their OCD-free full siblings. Follow-up began at the index date (OCD diagnosis or matching date) and continued until an incident cancer diagnosis, death, emigration, or end of follow-up (December 31, 2016, in Sweden, or 2015, in Denmark). To assess mortality risk in the Swedish population-matched cohort, individuals diagnosed with cancer were subsequently followed from cancer diagnosis until death, emigration, or end of follow-up. In the population-based matched cohorts, 1,372 (2.4%) of 57,239 individuals with OCD and 30,376 (2.7%) of 1,144,780 unaffected individuals developed cancer. OCD was not associated with overall cancer risk (pooled HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.94-1.04). In Sweden, OCD was associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.97) and melanoma (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.51-0.89). Following a cancer diagnosis, individuals with OCD showed no clear difference in cancer-specific mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.97-1.25), but showed higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.14-1.42), compared with individuals without OCD. OCD was not associated with overall cancer risk or cancer-specific mortality. However, it was associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after cancer diagnosis. There does not seem to be a higher-than-expected cancer burden in this population. However, the higher all-cause mortality after a cancer diagnosis suggests that clinical attention should be directed toward managing comorbid conditions to bridge the mortality gap.

title: Dsg2 arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is accompanied by neocortical synaptic changes in adult mice.
abstract: Heart failure is frequently accompanied by cognitive impairment, yet structural correlates in the brain remain incompletely defined. Here, we assessed whether chronic heart failure is associated with synaptic ultrastructural remodeling in the murine neocortex using a mouse model of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy caused by a point mutation in desmoglein-2 (Dsg2-W2A). Brains from aged adult homozygous Dsg2-W2A mice and age-matched wildtype controls were processed for transmission electron microscopy, and excitatory synapses in layer I of the prefrontal cortex were quantitatively assessed, with comparative analyses in the somatosensory cortex. In the prefrontal cortex, presynaptic terminal area and synaptic vesicle number were reduced in mutant mice, whereas postsynaptic measures were not altered. The prevalence of mitochondria and the spine apparatus within synapses was comparable between genotypes, suggesting no major loss of synapse-associated organelles. Finally, synaptic parameters in the prefrontal cortex did not show a systematic dependence on distance to local blood vessels. Together, these findings indicate moderate region- and compartment-specific synaptic ultrastructural alterations associated with Dsg2 cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure, with predominant effects on presynaptic terminals.

title: Palliative care knowledge and attitudes toward end-of-life care among clinical nurses across healthcare settings in Guangzhou, China: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Despite growing global recognition of palliative care's importance, access to adequately trained professionals and high-quality services remains highly unequal across countries. Nurses' knowledge and attitudes are critical determinants of end-of-life care quality, yet evidence from diverse institutional settings in China remains limited. This study aimed to assess palliative care knowledge and attitudes toward end-of-life care among nurses in Guangzhou, China, and to identify the key factors influencing these attitudes. This cross-sectional study recruited 1196 registered nurses from 17 institutions across seven administrative districts of Guangzhou between January 2019 and June 2023 using convenience sampling. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Palliative Care Quiz for Nursing (PCQN), and the Frommelt Attitudes Toward Care of the Dying Scale Form-B (FATCOD-B). Multiple linear regression was performed to identify independent predictors of attitudes toward end-of-life care. The sample included nurses from tertiary general (n = 424, 35.5%), oncology (n = 359, 30.0%), and community hospitals (n = 413, 34.5%). The overall PCQN accuracy rate was 53.2%, with the highest correct rate in the domain of "pain and other symptom control" (60.5%) and the lowest in "psychosocial support" (29.7%). The mean FATCOD-B score was 99.63 ± 8.56. Community hospital nurses scored lower on both knowledge and attitude measures. Multiple linear regression identified four independent predictors of end-of-life care attitudes: higher PCQN scores were associated with more positive attitudes (B = 5.593, P = 0.033); perceiving palliative care training as unnecessary was associated with less positive attitudes (B = - 5.620, P < 0.001); an ordinary (vs. harmonious) relationship with patients' families was associated with less positive attitudes (B = - 1.565, P = 0.009); and working in community hospitals was associated with lower FATCOD-B scores than working in tertiary general hospitals (B = - 1.641, P = 0.007). Nurses' palliative care knowledge was inadequate and attitudes toward end-of-life care remained suboptimal, particularly among nurses working in community hospitals. These findings underscore the need for systematic, institutionally tailored palliative care education and training, especially in community settings, to improve palliative care knowledge and foster more positive attitudes toward end-of-life care.

title: Understanding Australian health professionals' knowledge of concussion: a cross-sectional nationwide survey.
abstract: Concussion is a common condition following head injury affecting people across the lifespan. The purpose of this study was to understand the current state of concussion knowledge held by Australian health professionals, namely medical, nursing and allied health professionals. The primary aim was to establish health professionals' knowledge of concussion, specifically its: (i) mechanisms of injury; (ii) symptoms; (iii) management; (iv) differential diagnosis; (v) consequences; and vi) to determine the current frequency and type of care provided to concussion patients. An electronic survey was conducted. Participants included Australian health professionals who had worked in a professional capacity in the last 12-months. Convenience sampling was used for nationwide data collection over a 9-month period disseminated via email (e.g. through professional associations) and social media, allowing for snowballing. Quantitative methods of analysis were primarily adopted, supplemented by qualitative content analysis for free text responses. There were 126 participants (survey completion rate, 58%), who were most frequently female (n = 98/126, 78%), had more than 10 years of health professional experience (n = 88/126, 69%), and were aged between 30 and 39 years (n = 38/126, 30%). Participants were physiotherapists (n = 39/126, 31%), occupational therapists (n = 23/126, 18%), nurses (n = 17/126, 14%), medical professionals (including General Practitioners (GPs), physicians) (n = 13/126, 10%) and other health professionals (n = 20/126, 16%). Most participants correctly identified concussion injury mechanisms (n = 85/126, 68%); few participants correctly identified all concussion symptoms (n = 30/126, 24%); half the participants indicated they would frequently rely on published concussion management guidelines to inform practice (n = 65/126, 52%); differential diagnoses was considered by health professionals to varying degrees (e.g. intracranial injury (n = 57/64, 89%), and only some health professionals reported knowledge of persistent post-concussion symptoms (n = 78/126, 62%). The frequency and type of care provided to patients with concussion varied, but most frequently involved weekly (n = 25/66), or monthly (n = 10/66, 15%) reviews/treatment, with onward referral to Emergency Medicine Specialists being frequent for diagnosis of concussion (n = 11/17, 65%), and to a GP for treatment within 3 months (n = 7/18, 39%). While most Australian health professionals understand the mechanisms of injury for concussion, a gap exists regarding concussion symptoms, differential diagnoses, consequences and management. These gaps form a framework for future targeted education opportunities for health professionals who provide care to patients with a suspected or actual concussion.

title: Mitochondrial 'Attack-and-Trap' strategy potentiates cGAS-STING signaling to stimulate durable antitumor immunity against glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) recurrence, driven by therapeutic resistance and diffuse infiltration, remains a critical clinical challenge, fundamentally sustained by a mitochondrial metabolic addiction. To leverage this, we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform (HM-NPs@CM) camouflaged with cancer cell-mitochondria hybrid membranes. This ensures efficient blood-brain barrier traversal and precise mitochondria-targeted co-delivery of sonosensitizer Ce6 and mitophagy inhibitor Mdivi-1 within orthotopic GBM. Upon ultrasound activation, the nanoplatform executes a synergistic 'Attack-and-Trap' strategy: sonodynamic therapy (SDT) launches a targeted oxidative assault, while concurrent pharmacological inhibition of mitophagy traps irreparably damaged mitochondria. This accumulation of damaged mitochondria triggers a lethal pathological cascade, where mitochondrial oxidative stress progresses into severe intracellular oxidative stress, culminating in irreversible lytic cell death and sustained cytosolic mtDNA leakage. The liberated mtDNA robustly activates the cGAS-STING pathway, driving Type I interferon synthesis and transforming tumor cells into immunogenic reservoirs. Subsequently, this severe oxidative stress forces the terminal rupture of the plasma membrane, orchestrating the massive release of pre-synthesized immune effectors and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Capitalizing on these signals, combination with anti-PD-L1 blockade potently induces dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration, significantly suppressing tumor growth. Ultimately, this multimodal strategy establishes durable immunological memory, providing comprehensive protection against tumor rechallenge and post-surgical recurrence.

title: Weaning critically ill children undergoing prolonged sedation: challenges in achieving standardized practice.
abstract: The aim of this study was to observe how drug dose reduction and interruption is conducted in critically ill children receiving sedation for longer than 5 days, analyzed as drug dose percentage modifications relative to the first day of weaning. We also assessed adherence to a predefined tapering target between 10 and 20% of the initial sedative dose. Retrospective cohort study in a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). Overall, 41 patients were enrolled. The cohort median (interquartile range) daily percentage reductions during the weaning phase were 10.6% (3.8-20.4) for fentanyl, 3.3% (0-13.7) for midazolam, 0% (0-10.7) for dexmedetomidine, 5.4% (0-15.4) for ketamine, and 10.5% (0-20.0) for propofol. Median reductions were significantly lower from the 20% target for midazolam, dexmedetomidine, ketamine, and propofol, while fentanyl showed a borderline difference. Adherence to the scheduled tapering range (10-20%) was low across all sedatives during weaning phase. Fentanyl had the highest proportion of weaning days within the target range (19.8%). Overall, only 16 (39%) patients had Withdrawal Assessment Tool 1 (WAT-1) data. Of these, 8 (50%) were positive on the first day of evaluation and three (18%) on the last day. In children sedated for more than 5 days the recommended weaning rate was rarely respected. Withdrawal monitoring was suboptimal and did not guide drug weaning.

title: Shenfu Injection attenuates isoproterenol-induced heart failure partly through modulation of the TNF-α/TNFR1/NF-κB signaling pathway.
abstract: Shenfu injection (SFI) is widely used for heart failure (HF), but its cardioprotective mechanism remains incompletely understood. In this study, an isoproterenol-induced HF rat model, H9c2 cell injury model, network pharmacology, GEO analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were integrated to explore the mechanism of SFI. In rats, SFI improved cardiac function, with the medium-dose group increasing LVEF from 62.03 ± 5.89% in the ISO group to 79.33 ± 2.62% and LVFS from 29.68 ± 3.97% to 43.03 ± 2.49%. SFI also reduced NT-proBNP, inflammatory cytokines, and myocardial apoptosis. In H9c2 cells, 4‰ SFI improved ISO-induced cell injury and reduced apoptosis and inflammatory responses. Network pharmacology and GEO analysis indicated enrichment of the TNF signaling pathway, and molecular simulation suggested potential interactions between candidate SFI-related compounds and targets in the TNF-α/TNFR1/NF-κB axis. These findings suggest that SFI attenuates HF-related cardiac injury partly by suppressing inflammation and apoptosis through modulation of the TNF-α/TNFR1/NF-κB signaling pathway.
keywords: Receptors, Tumor Necrosis Factor, Type I

title: Awareness and use of a free vapes programme for smoking cessation in England: findings from the 2024 ITC 4 Country Smoking and Vaping Survey.
abstract: England's 'Swap to Stop' programme provides local authorities with free vape starter kits for adults who smoke. This study aimed to evaluate the reach, uptake, and correlates of engagement with Swap to Stop within the first year after the start of implementation. Our sample were adults (n = 2009) who currently smoke or recently stopped smoking from the England arm of the 2024 International Tobacco Control Four Country Smoking and Vaping Survey. We calculated weighted proportions for Swap to Stop awareness, offer, interest, and participation, and reasons for no interest/participation. We performed weighted binary logistic regressions to explore associations between sociodemographics, health, smoking cessation attempts, and vaping status and Swap to Stop awareness, offer, and interest/participation, and between interest/participation and vaping harm perceptions. Overall, 11.0% had heard of Swap to Stop, of whom 43.6% were offered to take part. Among those offered, 63.2% had participated; among those not offered, 55.1% were interested. The most common reasons for no interest/participation were not being interested in vapes (60.7%) and believing them to be unsafe (57.5%) or no less harmful than smoking (56.6%). Awareness was higher among non-White than White participants (AOR = 1.86), those with high (AOR = 1.78) and medium (AOR = 1.89) than lower incomes, and those who did than did not currently vape (AOR = 3.44), and lower among women than men (AOR = 0.57) and those aged ≥ 40 than ≤ 24 years (AOR = 0.28) and 25-39 years (AOR = 0.34). Offer of participation was also lower among those aged ≥ 40 years (AOR = 0.06 vs. ≤24 years, AOR = 0.21 vs. 25-39 years). Interest/participation was higher among people with than without prior smoking cessation attempts (AOR = 2.52) and among people who were than were not currently vaping (AOR = 4.50), and lower among women than men (AOR = 0.32). Interest/participation was associated with perceiving vaping as less harmful than smoking (AOR = 2.61). Within its first year, across England, awareness of Swap to Stop was limited, though uptake and interest in the programme were high. Awareness may have been higher in areas that adopted the programme early and may increase with maturation. Targeted outreach and communication on the relative harms of vaping is key to maximising public health impact.

title: An impaired excitatory-inhibitory balance in the right inferior temporal gyrus of patients with Alzheimer's disease correlated with executive function.
abstract: Preliminary research indicates that an imbalance between excitation and inhibition may be an early pathological feature of Alzheimer's disease. However, the relevant brain networks, neurotransmitters and genetic mechanisms are still unclear. This study enrolled 27 patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), 86 patients with mild cognitive impairment MCI, and 85 healthy controls (HC), all aged 65 or older, from the ADNI3 cohort in May 2024. We employed analysis of covariance to compare abnormalities in the excitation-inhibition balance across the three groups. We performed a transcriptomic analysis of abnormal excitation-inhibition imbalance. To elucidate the characteristics of the underlying brain networks, we extracted brain regions exhibiting differences in the balance of excitation and inhibition for seed-based functional connectivity analysis. Compared to the HC group, AD exhibits a significant putative excitatory-inhibitory imbalance in the right inferior temporal gyrus and superior orbital frontal gyrus. The Hurst exponent of the right inferior temporal gyrus was significantly correlated with executive function. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the abnormal excitation-inhibition imbalance observed in AD patients is significantly associated with GABA and mGluR5 receptors, as well as with genes that are enriched in the GABAergic synapse pathway. Functional connectivity analysis using the right inferior temporal gyrus as a seed point revealed significant abnormalities in the frontoparietal control network in AD patients. Our findings suggest that an imbalance between excitation and inhibition in the inferior temporal gyrus is a potential pathological mechanism underlying AD. This imbalance also leads to functional abnormalities in the frontoparietal control network associated with executive functions.

title: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
abstract: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

title: Evaluation of parents' awareness about the serious danger related to disc battery ingestion in children.
abstract: Disc battery (DB) ingestion is a potentially life-threatening pediatric emergency that requires prompt recognition, timely medical evaluation and urgent management to prevent severe complications. This study aimed to evaluate parents' awareness and knowledge of the risks associated with pediatric DB ingestion. A cross-sectional, survey-based study was conducted between March 1 and July 31, 2024, at Santobono-Pausilipon Children's Hospital (Naples, Italy), and at the offices of four primary care pediatricians in Italy. We submitted a 14-item questionnaire to 250 parents of children followed-up for well-child visits and subsequently analysed pooled data derived from their answers. 209/250 (83.6%) parents do not recognize DBs as a dangerous foreign body whenever ingested. Among the different kind of commercially available batteries, only 50/250 (20%) parents consider DBs as the most dangerous. 181/250 (72.4%) parents never heard about the possible risks related to DBs ingestion. Of those who responded that they had heard about the topic, 9/69 (13%) parents claim to have been informed by their pediatrician. In addition, 172/250 (68.8%) parents state that they have never implemented preventive measures at home. Our data show a very impressive lack of parental knowledge about the risk associated with DB ingestion in children. Many cases of ingestion could probably be prevented if large-scale information campaigns would increase the general population awareness about this source of serious danger to the health and even life of children. Not applicable.

title: Salience-limbic-cerebellar network reconfiguration during nitroglycerin-triggered cluster headache attacks.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Cluster headache is one of the most painful known disorders. Cluster headache sufferers compare the extreme unilateral pain to labour pains and gunshot wounds. Given the many logistical challenges of capturing spontaneous cluster headache attacks, only a handful of neuroimaging studies have successfully captured such attacks. Intravenous nitroglycerin (NTG) reliably induces cluster headache attacks in a controlled setting, thereby enabling investigation of resting-state functional connectivity during the attack stage. Cluster headache patients aged 18-60 years were recruited from both the population and tertiary headache clinics. Consented participants received either 0.5 µg/kg/min NTG or placebo infusion for 20 min. Structural T1, T2 and FLAIR sequences and resting state blood oxygen level dependent contrast (BOLD) time series were obtained at baseline (pre-infusion) and during headache. A total of 16 paired headache (NTG-infusion) and placebo scans were analysed. The functional connectivity was assessed for three pre-determined seeds: thalamus, ACC and insula. A two-factor (time and treatment), repeated measures 2 × 2 ANOVA model was used to assess main effects and interactions. Significant changes in functional connectivity between the contralateral amygdala (T = 3.47, peak connectivity change at 30, 0, -20, P < 0.001), and hippocampus (T = 4.33, peak connectivity change at 28, -8, -20, P < 0.001) and ipsilateral cerebellum culmen (T = 5.13, peak connectivity change at -14, -30, -18, P < 0.001), with respect to the anterior insula ipsilateral to the pain side. These findings suggest reconfiguration of salience, limbic, cerebellar and default mode networks during the cluster headache attack state and implicate the cerebellum in trigeminal nociceptive processing.

title: Improvement of Genome Editing Efficiency in Mammalian Cells by a Refined Uni-Vector Prime Editing System.
abstract: Prime editing is an advanced technology in the CRISPR/Cas genome editing field. The original multi-vector method utilized in prime editing has less efficiency and precision and is also inherently difficult in generating homozygous mutations in mammalian cells. To overcome these technical difficulties, a Uni-vector prime editing system containing the major components for prime editing has been constructed in two all-in-one plasmids, pPE3-pPuro and pePE5max-pPuro. The Uni-vector prime editing plasmids enhance the editing efficiency of prime editing and improve the generation of homozygous mutated mammalian cell lines. The editing efficiency depends on the transfection efficiency. Remarkably, the Uni-vector ePE5max system can achieve a high editing rate even in cell lines that are traditionally difficult to transfect. This Uni-vector approach simplifies the delivery of all the necessary editing components and greatly improves the editing efficiency. This approach represents an advanced progress in the field of prime editing.

title: The expansion of kinase drug discovery: new targets, platforms and indications.
abstract: In the past 25 years, kinase drug discovery has grown into one of the most thriving areas in pharmaceutical research and development. What began as a field dominated by ATP-competitive small molecules has diversified into a broad therapeutic landscape that includes allosteric and covalent inhibitors, activators, proximity-induced modulators, targeted protein degraders and antibody-based therapies, with more than 150 regulatory approvals so far worldwide. In this Review, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the current kinase therapeutic landscape, including more than 2,100 kinase-targeting agents that have entered clinical development in more than 23,000 clinical trials. We cover drug platforms, new targeting approaches, the expanding target spectrum, approvals and clinical trends. Nearly half of the canonical human protein kinases have at least one clinical-stage agent, placing kinases among the most intensively explored drug target classes. Nevertheless, development remains highly concentrated around a small set of blockbuster kinase targets, such as EGFR. We also examine the features associated with successful kinase-targeting agents and causes of agent discontinuations and regulatory withdrawal.

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss.
abstract: TDP-43 nuclear depletion is a defining pathological feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia that induces widespread cryptic splicing defects in hundreds of transcripts1-8. Despite this, whether TDP-43 loss affects synaptic function has remained unclear. Here we show that TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact but suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A was sufficient to rescue these deficits. We developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct UNC13A cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons and in a humanized mouse model. In human neurons this intervention restored spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses and wider network synchrony. Together, this establishes UNC13A splice correction as a mechanistically defined and genetically validated therapeutic strategy relevant to roughly 97% of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and roughly 50% of patients with frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 pathology.

title: Neuroprotective effects of combination of ezetimibe and sericin against lead-induced neurotoxicity.
abstract: Chronic exposure to environmental pollutants, particularly heavy metals, has become a global health concern, reducing longevity. Among these, lead (Pb2+) is associated with neurobehavioral, neurodevelopmental, and neuropsychological impairments. Consequently, growing interest focuses on pharmacological and natural agents that restore neurotrophic signaling. Therefore, this study investigates neuroprotective effect of ezetimibe, an anti-hyperlipidemic agent, and sericin, a natural protein, in Pb2+-induced neurotoxicity in rats. Adult Wistar rats were divided into seven groups: control, lead acetate (PbAc2; 50 mg/kg), ezetimibe (10 and 20 mg/kg), sericin (200 and 400 mg/kg), and a combination of ezetimibe (10 mg/kg) and sericin (200 mg/kg) with PbAc2. PbAc2 was administered for 55 days, while ezetimibe and sericin treatment was initiated on days 29-55. Behavioral assessments, including grip strength, open field test, and Morris water maze test, were performed. On day 56, animals were sacrificed, and hippocampal tissues were collected for neurochemical (GABA, GAD1, and dopamine) and mitochondrial complex 3 estimation, along with hippocampal histology. The qRT-PCR (Bax, Bcl2, caspase - 3, CREB, BDNF), western blot (IGF-1R, GLP-1R, PI3K, pAkt) were performed.
