The results demonstrated that PbAc2 exposure induced behavioral deficits, neurotransmitter imbalance, disrupted mitochondrial-associated apoptotic pathway, and impaired neurotrophin signaling. Contrarily, ezetimibe and sericin, individually and in combination, significantly attenuated neurobehavioral impairments, restored neurochemical levels, improved mitochondrial complex III activity, suppressed apoptotic signaling, and preserved hippocampal histoarchitecture and enhanced synaptic plasticity through involvement of IGF-1R/GLP-1R signaling pathway. These findings suggest that ezetimibe and sericin, in combination, represent promising therapeutic candidates for mitigating PbAc2-induced neurotoxicity.

title: International multidisciplinary Delphi consensus on advanced practice in non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (IMPACT UTUC).
abstract: Non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is characterized by limited high-level evidence and substantial heterogeneity in clinical practice across diagnosis, staging and treatment, highlighting the need for expert-driven guidance to reduce variability and improve patient outcomes. To address this gap, we conducted the international multidisciplinary Delphi consensus on advanced practice in non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma (IMPACT UTUC). This two-round, web-based Delphi survey involved 73 international UTUC experts (urologists and medical oncologists) from Europe, the Americas and Asia. A total of 40 statements covering two domains (diagnosis and staging, and treatment) were rated on a 9-point Likert scale, with predefined thresholds for consensus agreement and disagreement. Overall, consensus was achieved for 32 of 40 statements (80%) across both rounds. IMPACT UTUC provides the first structured international Delphi consensus spanning the entire non-metastatic UTUC care pathway, offering pragmatic expert-informed recommendations that could guide current clinical practice and inform the design of future prospective studies.

title: New culprit in early Alzheimer's: Blood-brain barrier blocks protective proteins.
Strain-Specific Reduction of Ndel1 Enzymatic Activity During Early Zika Virus Infection in the Neonatal Brain.
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during early development is associated with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including congenital microcephaly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking viral exposure to neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development. Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKVBR), an African lineage strain (ZIKVAF), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKVBR-infected animals, whereas ZIKVAF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7. Although both ZIKV strains induced robust inflammatory gene expression, only ZIKVBR infection resulted in decreased Ndel1 activity, dissociating neuroinflammatory signaling from enzymatic modulation. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKVBR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKVBR-associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

title: Are cueing effects really "negligible" when accuracy is emphasized and single masks eliminate uncertainty about target location?
abstract: Does spatial attention operate primarily by minimizing decision-related noise or by enhancing information from the attended location? While emphasizing and only reporting accuracy, Shiu and Pashler (Journal of Experimental Psychology. Human Perception and Performance, 20 (5), 1037-1054, 1994) found "negligible" effects of spatial pre-cues when uncertainty about the target's location was eliminated by a single mask, a finding often cited in favor of the idea that spatial pre-cues improve performance by reducing uncertainty (and not by signal enhancement). In a similar, single-mask condition, and while emphasizing reaction time (RT), Prasad and Hommel (Experimental Psychology, 71 (3):135-143, 2024), found significant cueing effects in reaction time and accuracy, which is consistent with signal enhancement. Stimulated by this empirical discrepancy, we implemented the fundamental methods of these studies to explore how invalid versus valid cues affected participant RT and accuracy. In each of two experiments we included a speed-stress manipulation: emphasizing response speed in one group and accuracy in the other. In Experiment 1, clear cueing effects were found in RT and accuracy across all conditions. In Experiment 2, with randomized single- and multiple-mask trials rather than blocked, the consistent cueing effects found in E1 were generally supported. Importantly, regardless of speed versus accuracy emphasis, we found robust cueing effects in the single-mask condition in both RT and accuracy. Whereas our results support signal enhancement as one mechanism of cueing effects, we acknowledge that multiple mechanisms may be operating to affect performance in a Posner-style cueing paradigm.
